items.appliesWhen: You name the type explicitly, e.g. in a variable or a helper that builds the messages object. Calling toast.promise(p, {...}) inline needs no change - T is inferred.
items.pitfall: The parameter defaults to unknown, so an un-parameterised annotation still compiles - and still hands your success callback `unknown`, which is the defect. Passing the type is what fixes it, not the compile.
items.verify: A success callback receives the resolved value with its real type: toast.promise(loadOrder(), { success: (order) => `Saved #${order.id}` }) compiles without a cast.
items.note: promise<T> declared a type parameter and then threw it away, because the messages interface hardcoded unknown. Every call site that wanted the resolved value had to cast.
items.action: Annotate as ToastPromiseMessages<T> where you name the type; inline object literals need no change.

informational: Typing on a closed ds-select now commits the type-ahead jump, as a native <select> does. The path existed but was unreachable, so nothing that worked before changes. NO ACTION.
A chip row's guard against a parent that hugs its content was unreachable and is removed; the measurement is unchanged. NO ACTION.

ToastService now shows at most 5 toasts at once by default, where it was previously unlimited. Extras queue and appear as earlier ones dismiss, so nothing is lost. Set DS_TOAST_CONFIG maxVisible to any other number, or 0 for no cap. The stack also animates when a toast is added rather than jumping; --ds-toast-shift-duration and --ds-toast-shift-easing tune that.

Toast announcements moved off the visual toast and onto the CDK LiveAnnouncer, so info, success and loading toasts are now announced at all — previously only error and warning were, and only by luck. Nothing to change if you use ToastService. If you render <ds-toast> directly it no longer carries role or aria-live and is silent to a screen reader: that markup is a specimen, and anything that should be announced should go through the service.
